# Grid Risk Command Center (Grid Equipment Failure & Outage Advisor)

> An operator-facing decision-support console for electricity utilities. It predicts
> which grid assets (transformers, substations, feeders, switchgear, circuit breakers)
> are likely to fail, explains why, ranks them by real-world consequence, simulates
> what happens if they do fail, and lets a control-room operator act on it — dispatch
> a crew, schedule or defer a job, or pre-position crews ahead of severe weather.

## Important context

- **All data is simulation data.** There is no live SCADA/IoT connection. Sensor
  telemetry, weather, incidents and crews are generated from a latent asset-health
  model by a seed script. Every figure in the UI is labelled as simulation data.
- **This is an internal, authenticated operator console**, not a public website or a
  storefront. It sits behind a login and is not intended to be crawled or indexed.
- It was built as a hackathon submission (IBM Bob AI Innovation Hackathon, team Nirmaan).

## What it does

- **Predict** — LightGBM classifier over 28 engineered features plus an IsolationForest
  anomaly score, trained on a time-aware held-out split. The live model metrics
  (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, precision, recall, F1) are reported by the app itself at
  `/api/model/metrics` rather than hardcoded.
- **Explain** — per-asset SHAP attributions surfaced as human-readable risk drivers,
  e.g. "partial-discharge rise (72h)".
- **Prioritise** — a Grid Impact Score (0–100) blending failure probability,
  asset criticality, customers served, downstream network exposure and weather risk.
  Raw failure probability alone is a poor ranking signal; this is what drives the
  maintenance queue.
- **Simulate** — what-if modelling for a single asset failure or a severe weather
  event, returning customers affected, downstream assets, nearest crew and estimated
  outage duration.
- **Act** — dispatch, schedule, defer, pre-position and acknowledge actions write real
  work orders, change crew availability, and are recorded in an audit log.

## AI copilot

The operations copilot answers operator questions using only real backend tool results
and cites the tool calls behind each answer. It runs against the IBM Bob CLI in headless
mode (`bob run --mode ask`) when `BOB_API_KEY` is configured, falls back to IBM
watsonx.ai or another configured provider, and otherwise falls back to a deterministic
grounded router that answers from the same tools without a language model. It never
invents asset ids, probabilities or customer counts.

## Tech stack

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn
- Data: SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`, no ORM)
- ML: pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM, SHAP
- Frontend: build-free static SPA — vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind (CDN), Leaflet, Chart.js
- No React, no bundler, no build step
